To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
consumer–green brand relationship quality is positively related to consumer value perceptions, consumer satisfaction and loyalty.
consumer value is the key to understanding consumer–brand relationship and consumer loyalty.

(1) there are three types of value and four types of cost that are associated with consumer–green brand relationship, (2) the value and cost of the relationship are influenced by the psychographic characteristics of the consumer, and (3) there are several relationships between the value, cost and the dimensions of relationship quality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a conceptual framework for the analysis of the value and cost of green brands, and their relationship with consumer behaviour and loyalty.
the development of a CV framework that may be applied in the green brands context and may provide a better understanding of the value and costs of green brands, as well as RQ and loyalty.
the development and testing of the proposed conceptual model in order to understand the factors that affect consumer–green brand relationship development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the article contributes to the development of the CV concept in a novel context, and to the understanding of green consumer behaviour.
the CV framework proposed in this article is a valuable tool to understand the factors that influence consumer behaviour towards green products.
this conceptual article provides a framework for future research on the development and maintenance of consumer–green brands relationship.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a conceptual framework that provides a better understanding of how consumers value and cost green brands, as well as what are the dimensions of RQL and loyalty that are the most relevant for the consumer–green brand relationship.
this paper is the first one that applies the concept of CV in the green marketing literature and proposes a conceptual framework for the development of consumer- green brands relationship.
the proposed conceptual framework may be used as a starting point for the development of a more complete and comprehensive model, which can be tested empirically in future research studies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
green consumers are not a homogenous group, and that their behaviour is driven by a complex set of factors that are related to their values, attitudes, perceptions, and psychographic characteristics.
the value–cost–RQ–loyalty chain is not a linear process, and that the value and cost factors are not the sole drivers of RQ and consumer loyalty.
green marketing is an important area of research that can benefit from the application of existing theories from the fields of CV, relationship and environmental marketing.
